clues: When God appeared to me in a dream asking what I wanted, I asked for wisdom to govern his people.

items.x: Solomon was renowned throughout the ancient world for God-given wisdom, magnificent wealth, and constructing the Temple in Jerusalem.

clues: I was one of only two spies who brought back an encouraging report after scouting Canaan.

clues: An angel announced to my mother that no razor was ever to come upon my head.

items.x: Samson was a Nazirite judge of immense physical power who judged Israel for twenty years and defeated thousands of Philistines.

clues: I served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes in the royal fortress of Susa.

If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.
He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
We love him, because he first loved us.
Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,
I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.

clues: I was married to a priest who lived to be an hundred and thirty years old.
My brother was a king of Judah slain in the days of Jehu.
I stole a baby prince away and hid him with his nurse in a bedchamber.
My nephew Joash was kept hidden in the house of the LORD six years, then crowned at seven.
items.x: Jehosheba, wife of the priest Jehoiada, hid the infant Joash from Athaliah until he could be made king.

clues: God promised that my life would be 'for a prey' unto me, because I put my trust in Him.
I was a eunuch in the house of King Zedekiah.
I took thirty men with me to rescue a prophet.
I let down old cast clouts and rotten rags so the prophet could be drawn up out of the dungeon.
items.x: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian drew Jeremiah out of the miry dungeon, and God promised to deliver him.

clues: My husband Shallum was keeper of the wardrobe.
I dwelt in Jerusalem in the college.
A priest, a scribe and others came to me after a book of the law was found in the house of the LORD.
I told King Josiah he would be gathered to his grave in peace.
items.x: Huldah the prophetess confirmed the words of the found book of the law to Josiah's messengers.

clues: King David told me I was a stranger and an exile who came 'but yesterday'.
Six hundred men came after the king from Gath.
I swore that in death or life, wherever the king was, there would I be.
David put a third part of his people under my hand against Absalom.
items.x: Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner, refused to leave David when he fled from Absalom.

clues: I came to meet a fleeing king with my coat rent and earth upon my head.
I was called the king's friend.
I went into Absalom's court pretending to serve him.
My counsel was preferred over the counsel of Ahithophel.
items.x: Hushai the Archite defeated Ahithophel's counsel so that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.

clues: I was the daughter of Aiah.
A captain named Abner was accused of going in unto me.
Two of my sons were hanged by the Gibeonites.
I spread sackcloth on a rock and kept birds and beasts from their bodies, from harvest until rain.
items.x: Rizpah, Saul's concubine, guarded the bodies of her sons, and David then buried Saul's house.

clues: I lived at Lodebar in the house of Machir.
I was five years old when my nurse fell with me as she fled.
I called myself a dead dog before the king.
Though lame on both feet, I ate continually at the king's table.
items.x: David showed kindness to Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, for Jonathan's sake.

clues: My father promised me as wife to the man who took Kirjathsepher.
My husband later became the first judge of Israel after Joshua's generation.
I lighted off my ass to ask my father for a blessing.
I asked for springs of water and was given the upper and the nether springs.
items.x: Achsah, Caleb's daughter, married Othniel and asked her father for springs of water.

clues: I was a young man at Troas.
I sat in a window while a preacher continued his speech until midnight.
Fallen into a deep sleep, I fell down from the third loft.
The preacher embraced me and said, 'his life is in him.'
items.x: Eutychus fell from a window during Paul's long sermon and was brought back alive.

clues: Paul called me his brother, companion in labour, and fellowsoldier.
I was the Philippians' messenger, who ministered to Paul's wants.
I was sick nigh unto death, but God had mercy on me.
I carried the Philippians' gift to Paul, an odour of a sweet smell.
items.x: Epaphroditus nearly died serving Paul on behalf of the church at Philippi.

clues: Paul sent greetings to my household at the end of his last letter.
Paul prayed, 'The Lord give mercy unto the house' bearing my name.
I oft refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chain.
When I was in Rome, I sought Paul out very diligently and found him.
items.x: Onesiphorus searched for Paul in Rome and refreshed him in prison.

clues: My father was Carmi, of the tribe of Judah.
I saw a goodly Babylonish garment among the spoils.
I hid two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold in my tent.
I was stoned in a valley that was then called the valley of Achor.
items.x: Achan took of the accursed thing at Jericho, and Israel was defeated at Ai.

clues: My mother Zeruiah was the sister of a king.
I went up first against the Jebusites and so became chief and captain.
I killed Abner in the gate of Hebron.
I thrust three darts through the heart of Absalom as he hung in an oak.
items.x: Joab, David's captain, killed Absalom against the king's orders.

clues: I went down with David by night into Saul's camp.
I asked David to let me smite Saul to the earth with his own spear.
I wanted to take off the head of a man who cursed David.
I rescued David from the giant Ishbibenob.
items.x: Abishai, Joab's brother, saved David from Ishbibenob the Philistine giant.

clues: I was the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi.
A young prophet anointed me king in an inner chamber.
The watchman knew me from afar because I drove furiously.
I ordered a queen thrown down from a window.
items.x: Jehu was anointed to destroy the house of Ahab, and Jezebel was thrown down at his word.

clues: By me the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria.
A little captive maid told my wife about a prophet in Samaria.
I said Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, were better than all the waters of Israel.
After my healing, I asked for two mules' burden of earth.
items.x: Naaman the Syrian captain was healed of leprosy after dipping seven times in Jordan.

clues: I told my master that a kind woman had no child and her husband was old.
I laid my master's staff on a dead child's face, but there was neither voice nor hearing.
I ran after a Syrian captain and asked for a talent of silver and two changes of garments.
I went out from my master's presence a leper as white as snow.
items.x: Gehazi took a gift from Naaman by a lie, and Naaman's leprosy clave to him.

clues: I feared the LORD from my youth.
I was governor of the house of a wicked king.
When Jezebel cut off the prophets, I hid an hundred of them by fifty in a cave.
I met Elijah while searching the land for grass to save the horses and mules.
items.x: Obadiah, Ahab's steward, secretly protected a hundred prophets of the LORD.

clues: I was the son of Imlah.
A king said he hated me because I never prophesied good concerning him.
I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah smote me on the cheek.
items.x: Micaiah alone foretold Ahab's defeat at Ramothgilead, against four hundred false prophets.

clues: I feared God more than the king of Egypt.
I was commanded to kill every Hebrew son at birth.
I told Pharaoh that Hebrew women are lively and deliver before the midwives come.
My fellow midwife was named Puah.
items.x: Shiphrah and Puah, Hebrew midwives, saved the boys alive, and God dealt well with them.

clues: My husband Amram was my nephew: I was his father's sister.
I was a daughter of Levi, born in Egypt.
I hid my baby son three months, then laid him in an ark of bulrushes.
I bore Aaron, Moses and Miriam.
items.x: Jochebed was the mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam.

clues: I was the daughter of Amminadab.
My brother Naashon was a prince of the tribe of Judah.
My husband was Israel's first high priest.
Two of my sons died before the LORD for offering strange fire.
items.x: Elisheba was Aaron's wife and the mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

clues: My grandfather was Aaron the priest.
I thrust a javelin through an Israelite man and a Midianitish woman.
My zeal stayed a plague in which twenty and four thousand died.
God gave me the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
items.x: Phinehas turned God's wrath away at Peor and received a covenant of peace.

clues: I was the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
God filled me with His spirit in wisdom to devise cunning works.
Aholiab of the tribe of Dan was appointed with me.
I made the ark of shittim wood.
items.x: Bezaleel was the Spirit-filled craftsman of the tabernacle and its furniture.

clues: I was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali.
My father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass.
I set up two pillars of brass called Jachin and Boaz.
I made a molten sea for Solomon's house of the LORD.
items.x: Hiram the brassworker from Tyre made the pillars and the molten sea for Solomon's temple.

clues: My husband's name meant folly, and folly was with him.
I brought two hundred loaves and two bottles of wine to six hundred men.
I hurried to meet David and kept him from shedding blood.
After my husband died, I became David's wife.
items.x: Abigail's wise intervention kept David from avenging himself on Nabal.

clues: I was very great: I had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats.
I was of the house of Caleb.
I answered, 'Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse?'
My heart died within me, and I became as a stone.
items.x: Nabal insulted David's men, and about ten days later the LORD smote him.

clues: I was a Gileadite from Rogelim.
I provided the king with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim.
At fourscore years old, I said I could no longer hear the voice of singing men.
I asked that my servant Chimham go over with the king instead of me.
items.x: Barzillai sustained David during Absalom's rebellion and declined to live at court.

clues: I was a servant of the house of Saul.
I had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
I met the fleeing king with asses, bread, raisins and a bottle of wine.
I told the king my master had stayed in Jerusalem hoping to receive his father's kingdom.
items.x: Ziba, Saul's servant, tilled the land for Mephibosheth and later accused him before David.

clues: I was of the family of the house of Saul, the son of Gera.
I threw stones and cast dust at a fleeing king, cursing him.
I was told to build a house in Jerusalem and never cross the brook Kidron.
I went to Gath to bring back two runaway servants, and it cost me my life.
items.x: Shimei cursed David, was spared, and later died for breaking Solomon's command.

clues: I was a man of Belial, a Benjamite.
I blew a trumpet and said, 'We have no part in David.'
I took refuge in Abel of Bethmaachah.
A wise woman had my head cut off and thrown over the wall to Joab.
items.x: Sheba son of Bichri led a revolt after Absalom's death, ended by a wise woman of Abel.

clues: My mother was Haggith.
My father had never displeased me by asking, 'Why hast thou done so?'
I exalted myself, saying, 'I will be king,' while my father was old.
I caught hold on the horns of the altar for fear of my brother.
items.x: Adonijah tried to seize the throne before David named Solomon king.

clues: I was a Shunammite.
I was chosen as a fair damsel sought throughout all the coasts of Israel.
I cherished an aged king and ministered to him, but the king knew me not.
A prince lost his life after asking that I be given him to wife.
items.x: Abishag cared for David in his old age; Adonijah's request for her led to his death.

clues: I was the son of Jehoiada, of Kabzeel.
I went down and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow.
I slew an Egyptian with his own spear.
Solomon put me over the host in Joab's place.
items.x: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was one of David's mighty men and later Solomon's commander.

clues: I was the son of Gera, a Benjamite.
I was a man lefthanded.
I made a dagger of a cubit length and girded it on my right thigh.
I delivered Israel from Eglon the king of Moab.
items.x: Ehud killed Eglon and Israel had rest fourscore years.

clues: In my days the highways were unoccupied.
I was the son of Anath.
I slew six hundred Philistines.
My weapon was an ox goad.
items.x: Shamgar delivered Israel with an ox goad.

clues: I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
A thirsty captain asked me for water, and I gave him milk.
I covered him with a mantle.
I drove a nail of the tent into his temples.
items.x: Jael killed Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army, fulfilling Deborah's word.

clues: I was the son of an harlot, and my brothers thrust me out.
I dwelt in the land of Tob, and vain men gathered to me.
The elders of Gilead asked me to be their captain against Ammon.
My only child came out to meet me with timbrels after I made a vow.
items.x: Jephthah the Gileadite delivered Israel from Ammon and kept a costly vow.

clues: My mother was a concubine in Shechem.
I slew my seventy brothers upon one stone.
My youngest brother told a parable of trees about me.
A woman cast a piece of a millstone upon my head.
items.x: Abimelech, Gideon's son, made himself king at Shechem and died at Thebez.

clues: I was the youngest son of Jerubbaal.
I survived the slaughter of my brothers because I hid myself.
From the top of mount Gerizim I told a parable in which the trees anoint a bramble.
Afterwards I ran away and dwelt in Beer.
items.x: Jotham's parable of the trees warned Shechem against making Abimelech king.

clues: I was a certain disciple at Damascus.
The Lord told me to go to the street which is called Straight.
I was afraid, because I had heard how much evil a man had done to the saints at Jerusalem.
I put my hands on a blind man and something like scales fell from his eyes.
items.x: Ananias of Damascus laid hands on Saul so that he received his sight and was filled with the Holy Ghost.

clues: I was a centurion of the band called the Italian band.
I was a devout man who gave much alms and prayed to God alway.
An angel told me to send men to Joppa for one Simon.
The Holy Ghost fell on my household while Peter was still speaking.
items.x: Cornelius, a Gentile centurion, and his household received the Holy Ghost and were baptized.

clues: I was of the city of Thyatira.
I was a seller of purple.
The Lord opened my heart at a riverside place of prayer.
After my household was baptized, I constrained Paul's company to abide in my house.
items.x: Lydia was the first recorded convert in Philippi.

clues: I lived at Joppa.
My name, by interpretation, is called Dorcas.
I was full of good works and almsdeeds, and made coats and garments for widows.
Peter knelt, prayed, and said my name, and I opened my eyes.
items.x: Peter raised Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead at Joppa.

clues: I was a Jew born at Alexandria.
I was an eloquent man, mighty in the scriptures.
I knew only the baptism of John until a couple expounded the way of God more perfectly.
Some at Corinth said, 'I am of' me, while others said 'I am of Paul.'
items.x: Apollos was taught by Aquila and Priscilla and watered what Paul planted at Corinth.

clues: I was a Jew born in Pontus.
I had lately come from Italy because Claudius commanded all Jews to depart from Rome.
I was a tentmaker by occupation, and Paul abode with me.
My wife and I expounded unto Apollos the way of God more perfectly.
items.x: Aquila and Priscilla worked with Paul as tentmakers and helped Apollos.

clues: The apostles sent me with Judas surnamed Barsabas to Antioch with a letter.
I was chosen as Paul's companion after Barnabas departed with Mark.
I was beaten and put in the stocks at Philippi.
At midnight I prayed and sang praises unto God with Paul in prison.
items.x: Silas travelled with Paul and sang with him in the Philippian jail.

clues: I was a Levite of the country of Cyprus.
The apostles surnamed me, which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation.
I sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
I brought a converted persecutor to the apostles at Jerusalem when they were afraid of him.
items.x: Barnabas (Joses) was a generous Levite from Cyprus who vouched for Saul.

clues: I was chosen as one of seven men of honest report to serve tables.
I was full of faith and power and did great wonders among the people.
False witnesses said I spoke against the temple and the law.
As I was stoned I saw the heavens opened and the Son of man standing at God's right hand.
items.x: Stephen, one of the seven, was the first recorded Christian martyr in Acts.

clues: I was one of the seven chosen to serve the widows.
I preached Christ in the city of Samaria.
An angel sent me to the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza.
I had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
items.x: Philip the evangelist preached in Samaria and baptized the Ethiopian eunuch.

clues: I was a prophet who came from Jerusalem unto Antioch.
I signified by the Spirit a great dearth throughout all the world.
That dearth came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.
I bound my own hands and feet with Paul's girdle to show what would happen to him.
items.x: Agabus foretold a famine and Paul's binding at Jerusalem.

clues: I was a damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark.
I came to hearken when someone knocked at the door of the gate.
I knew Peter's voice and, for gladness, opened not the gate.
The disciples told me I was mad when I said Peter stood outside.
items.x: Rhoda was so glad to hear Peter's voice that she left him knocking at the gate.

clues: I was a rich man and an honourable counsellor.
I had not consented to the counsel and deed of the council.
I went in boldly unto Pilate and craved a body.
I laid Jesus in my own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
items.x: Joseph of Arimathaea buried Jesus in his own new tomb.

clues: I was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews.
I came to Jesus by night.
I asked how a man can be born when he is old.
I brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight, for Jesus' burial.
items.x: Nicodemus heard Jesus teach the new birth and later helped bury Him.

clues: I was a priest of the course of Abia.
I was chosen by lot to burn incense in the temple of the Lord.
Because I did not believe Gabriel, I was dumb until the day his words were performed.
I wrote on a writing table, 'His name is John.'
items.x: Zacharias was the father of John the Baptist.

clues: I was a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel.
I was of the tribe of Aser.
I had lived with an husband seven years from my virginity.
I departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
items.x: Anna gave thanks for the infant Jesus and spoke of Him to all who looked for redemption.

clues: I was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
It was revealed to me that I would not see death before I had seen the Lord's Christ.
I came by the Spirit into the temple when the child Jesus was brought in.
I said, 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.'
items.x: Simeon took the infant Jesus in his arms and blessed God.

clues: I was one of the rulers of the synagogue.
My only daughter, about twelve years of age, lay dying.
On the way to my house, a woman with an issue of blood touched the Master.
Jesus took my daughter by the hand and said, 'Talitha cumi.'
items.x: Jesus raised the daughter of Jairus from the dead.

clues: I was the son of Timaeus.
I sat by the highway side begging as Jesus left Jericho.
Many charged me to hold my peace, but I cried the more.
I cast away my garment, rose, and came to Jesus.
items.x: Blind Bartimaeus received his sight and followed Jesus in the way.

clues: I was a servant of the high priest.
I came with a band and officers to a garden over the brook Cedron.
A disciple drew a sword and cut off my right ear.
My kinsman later asked Peter, 'Did not I see thee in the garden with him?'
items.x: Peter cut off Malchus' right ear at Jesus' arrest; Luke records that Jesus healed it.

clues: I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people.
I commanded that the apostles be put forth a little space.
I told the council that if this work were of God, they could not overthrow it.
Saul of Tarsus was brought up at my feet.
items.x: Gamaliel counselled the council to leave the apostles alone.

clues: My wife Drusilla was a Jewess.
Paul reasoned before me of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come.
I trembled and said, 'Go thy way for this time.'
I hoped that money would be given me by Paul, and left him bound for two years.
items.x: Felix the governor heard Paul but delayed his case hoping for a bribe.

clues: I succeeded Felix as governor.
I asked Paul if he would go up to Jerusalem to be judged before me.
Paul appealed unto Caesar while standing before my judgment seat.
I said with a loud voice, 'Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.'
items.x: Porcius Festus heard Paul's appeal to Caesar.

clues: I was a silversmith.
I made silver shrines for Diana.
I called together workmen of like occupation, warning that our craft was in danger.
My speech set a whole city crying, 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians.'
items.x: Demetrius stirred up the riot at Ephesus against Paul's preaching.

clues: I was a sorcerer and false prophet, a Jew.
My name was also Barjesus.
I was with the deputy Sergius Paulus and sought to turn him away from the faith.
Paul declared I would be blind for a season, and a mist and darkness fell on me.
items.x: Elymas opposed Paul on Cyprus and was struck blind for a season.

clues: I lived at Lydda.
I had kept my bed eight years.
I was sick of the palsy.
Peter said to me, 'Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed.'
items.x: All that dwelt at Lydda and Saron turned to the Lord after Aeneas was healed.

clues: I was of Asia and travelled with Paul.
Paul called me a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord.
I was sent to the Ephesians to make known Paul's affairs and comfort their hearts.
I carried word to Colosse together with Onesimus.
items.x: Tychicus carried Paul's news to Ephesus and Colosse.

clues: I was a servant of the church at Cenchrea.
Paul asked the Romans to receive me in the Lord, as becometh saints.
Paul asked them to assist me in whatsoever business I had need of.
I had been a succourer of many, and of Paul himself.
items.x: Paul commended Phebe of Cenchrea to the church in Rome.

clues: I loved to have the preeminence.
I received not the apostle John.
I prated against the brethren with malicious words.
I forbade those who would receive the brethren and cast them out of the church.
items.x: John rebuked Diotrephes for his pride and refusal to welcome the brethren.

clues: Paul once listed me with Luke as a fellowlabourer who sent greetings.
I was with Paul when he wrote to the Colossians.
Paul wrote that I forsook him.
I left because I loved this present world, and departed unto Thessalonica.
items.x: Demas, once Paul's fellowlabourer, forsook him for love of the world.

clues: I was the priest of Midian.
I had seven daughters, and one of them married Moses.
I came to Moses in the wilderness with his wife and two sons.
I advised Moses to appoint rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
items.x: Jethro counselled Moses to share the burden of judging the people.

clues: I was with Aaron and Moses on the top of the hill during the battle with Amalek.
I stayed up Moses' hands, one on one side and Aaron on the other.
Moses left Aaron and me in charge of the people while he went up the mount.
My grandson Bezaleel built the tabernacle.
items.x: Hur and Aaron held up Moses' hands so Israel prevailed against Amalek.

clues: I was the son of Beor, from Pethor.
A king offered me great honour to curse Israel.
An angel with a drawn sword stood in my way, and my ass saw him before I did.
Instead of cursing Israel, I blessed them three times.
items.x: Balaam was hired by Balak to curse Israel but could only speak what God gave him.

clues: I was the son of Jephunneh, of the tribe of Judah.
I was one of twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
I said, 'Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.'
At eighty-five, I was as strong as the day Moses sent me, and I asked for Hebron.
items.x: Caleb wholly followed the LORD and received Hebron as his inheritance.

clues: I was one of two wives of Elkanah.
My adversary provoked me sore because the LORD had shut up my womb.
A priest thought I was drunken as I prayed, for only my lips moved.
I lent my son to the LORD as long as he lived.
items.x: Hannah prayed for a son and gave Samuel to the LORD.

clues: I was a priest at Shiloh and judged Israel forty years.
I thought a praying woman was drunk.
My sons Hophni and Phinehas made themselves vile, and I restrained them not.
When I heard the ark of God was taken, I fell backward and my neck brake.
items.x: Eli the priest died when he heard the ark of God was taken.

clues: I was a Hittite and one of David's mighty men.
I would not go down to my house while the ark and Israel abode in tents.
I slept at the door of the king's house with the servants.
I carried my own death warrant to Joab.
items.x: Uriah, Bathsheba's husband, was set in the forefront of battle by David's letter.

clues: I was a Benjamite, the son of Jair.
I raised my uncle's daughter after her father and mother died.
I discovered two chamberlains plotting to lay hands on the king.
I would not bow nor do reverence to Haman.
items.x: Mordecai raised Esther and was later honoured by the king.

clues: I was the son of Neriah.
I wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD in a roll.
I read the roll in the house of the LORD on a fasting day.
The LORD told me, 'Seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not.'
items.x: Baruch was Jeremiah's scribe who wrote and read his prophecies.

items.q: The Bible says three wise men came to see the young child Jesus.
items.x: Matthew never gives their number. Three gifts are named (gold, frankincense, myrrh), which is where the 'three' tradition comes from.

items.q: The wise men found Jesus lying in the manger.
items.x: Matthew says they came 'into the house' and saw 'the young child'. The manger scene is the shepherds' visit in Luke 2.

items.q: Genesis says Eve ate an apple.
items.x: Genesis only calls it 'the fruit' of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. No kind of fruit is named.

items.q: The Bible says, 'Money is the root of all evil.'
items.x: Paul says 'the LOVE of money is the root of all evil', not money itself.

items.q: 'God helps those who help themselves' is a Bible verse.
items.x: The saying is not in Scripture. The Bible's message is that God helps those who are without strength.

items.q: God told Noah to take exactly two of every kind of animal, clean and unclean alike.
items.x: Clean beasts went in by sevens, the male and his female; unclean beasts went in by two.

items.q: Luke 8 describes Mary Magdalene as a woman who had been a prostitute.
items.x: The Bible says seven devils went out of her. It never calls her a prostitute; that idea came from later tradition.

items.q: 'Spare the rod and spoil the child' is a Bible verse, word for word.
items.x: Proverbs 13:24 says, 'He that spareth his rod hateth his son.' The rhyming phrase is a later proverb.

items.q: Isaiah prophesied that 'the lion shall lie down with the lamb.'
items.x: Isaiah 11:6 pairs the WOLF with the lamb and the leopard with the kid. The lion is with the calf and the fatling.

items.q: Moses led Israel across the river Jordan on dry ground.
items.x: Moses died before Israel entered Canaan. They crossed Jordan under Joshua, as the priests stood in the river with the ark.

items.q: The Bible says Jesus was born on December 25.
items.x: No date of Jesus' birth is given in Scripture.

items.q: The forbidden tree in Eden was the tree of life.
items.x: The forbidden tree was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The tree of life was guarded after the fall (Genesis 3:24).

items.q: Adam named his wife Eve before they ate the forbidden fruit.
items.x: Before the fall he called her 'Woman' (Genesis 2:23). He named her Eve after the fall, 'because she was the mother of all living'.

items.q: Jesus renamed Saul as Paul on the road to Damascus.
items.x: Acts keeps calling him Saul long after his conversion. The name Paul first appears at Paphos in Acts 13:9 with 'who also is called Paul'.

items.q: David cut off Goliath's head with his own sword.
items.x: David had no sword. He killed Goliath with a sling stone, then drew Goliath's own sword and cut off his head.

items.q: Moses carved and wrote the words on the first tables of stone with his own hand.
items.x: The first tables were 'written with the finger of God'.

items.q: The Bible gives the name of Noah's wife.
items.x: Noah's wife is mentioned but never named in Scripture.

items.q: Jesus is said to have been 33 years old when He began His ministry.
items.x: Luke says He 'began to be about thirty years of age'.

items.q: Scripture says Elijah rode the chariot of fire up into heaven.
items.x: The chariot of fire 'parted them both asunder'. Elijah 'went up by a whirlwind into heaven'.

items.q: Luke records the name of the thief on the cross who repented.
items.x: Neither thief is named in Scripture. Names like 'Dismas' come from later tradition.

items.q: Adam ate the forbidden fruit first and then gave it to Eve.
items.x: Eve ate first, then gave to her husband, who was with her.

items.q: Israel's forty years in the wilderness were God's judgment for the golden calf.
items.x: The forty years came after the spies' evil report and the people's unbelief: one year for each day of the search.

items.q: Every one of Jesus' twelve apostles was a fisherman.
items.x: Matthew was a tax collector (publican) when Jesus called him.

items.q: The Bible says Cain killed Abel with a rock.
items.x: Genesis says Cain slew Abel but does not say how.

items.q: The word 'apple' never appears in the King James Bible.
items.x: 'Apple' appears several times, e.g. Proverbs 25:11, 'the apple of his eye' (Deuteronomy 32:10) and the apple tree in Song of Solomon 2:3.

items.q: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a horse.
items.x: He rode a colt, the foal of an ass, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9.

items.q: The Bible says Peter was crucified upside down.
items.x: Jesus foretold Peter's death in John 21, but the upside-down crucifixion comes from later tradition, not Scripture.

items.q: The letter to the Hebrews names Paul as its writer.
items.x: The letter does not name its author anywhere in its text.

items.q: The last book of the Bible is called 'Revelations'.
items.x: It is 'The Revelation' (singular): 'The Revelation of Jesus Christ'.

items.q: Luke says the angels SANG to the shepherds at Jesus' birth.
items.x: Luke says the heavenly host was 'praising God, and saying'. It does not say they sang.

items.q: Luke tells us Mary rode a donkey to Bethlehem.
items.x: Luke says Joseph went up with Mary but mentions no donkey.

items.q: Luke says Jesus was born in a stable.
items.x: Luke mentions a manger and no room in the inn. The word 'stable' is not used.

items.q: Enoch died when he was 365 years old.
items.x: Enoch did not die: 'God took him'. Hebrews 11:5 says he was translated that he should not see death.

items.q: The Bible gives King Saul's exact height in cubits.
items.x: Saul was taller than everyone 'from his shoulders and upward', but no measurement is given. Goliath's height is the one given in cubits.

items.q: 'Pride comes before a fall' is a word-for-word Bible verse.
items.x: Proverbs says pride goes before DESTRUCTION, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

items.q: Jesus' brothers believed in Him during His ministry.
items.x: John says plainly that 'neither did his brethren believe in him'.

items.q: Peter and John took Jesus' body down from the cross.
items.x: Joseph of Arimathaea asked Pilate for the body, and Nicodemus came with him.

items.q: Noah's ark came to rest on Mount Sinai.
items.x: The ark rested 'upon the mountains of Ararat'.

items.q: Jesus fed the five thousand with seven loaves.
items.x: The five thousand were fed with five loaves and two fishes. Seven loaves fed the four thousand (Matthew 15:34-38).

items.q: Jonah prayed to God from inside the fish's belly.
items.x: Jonah 2 is his prayer 'out of the fish's belly'.

items.q: The Bible calls Jesus 'the carpenter'.
items.x: His hometown asked, 'Is not this the carpenter?' (Mark 6:3).

items.q: Methuselah lived 969 years.
items.x: Genesis 5:27 gives 969 years.

items.q: In the parable, the prodigal son's father ran to meet him.
items.x: While the son was 'yet a great way off', the father 'ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him'.

items.q: In the Good Samaritan parable, the wounded man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho.
items.x: Jesus says 'a certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves'.

items.q: John calls the water turned to wine at Cana Jesus' 'beginning of miracles'.
items.x: John 2:11 calls it the 'beginning of miracles'.

items.q: The ninth plague on Egypt was darkness.
items.x: Darkness for three days was the ninth plague. The death of the firstborn came tenth.

items.q: Joseph's coat is called a 'coat of many colours' in the KJV.
items.x: Genesis 37:3 KJV: 'he made him a coat of many colours'.

items.q: The book of Esther never once uses the word 'God' or 'LORD' in the KJV.
items.x: God's name does not appear in Esther, yet His providence runs through it: deliverance 'from another place'.

items.q: Psalm 117, with just two verses, is the shortest chapter in the Bible.
items.x: Psalm 117 has two verses, the fewest of any chapter.

items.q: Psalm 119 has 176 verses, the most of any chapter.
items.x: Psalm 119 has 176 verses: 22 sections of 8 verses.

items.q: Abraham's name was originally Abram.
items.x: God changed Abram's name to Abraham, 'a father of many nations'.

items.q: Goliath's height is given as six cubits and a span.
items.x: 1 Samuel 17:4 gives Goliath's height as six cubits and a span.

items.q: Judas was paid thirty pieces of silver to betray Jesus.
items.x: The chief priests covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

items.q: Jesus' first recorded words in Luke's Gospel were spoken when He was twelve.
items.x: At twelve, in the temple, Jesus said, 'wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?'

items.q: Ruth was a Moabitess.
items.x: Ruth is repeatedly called 'the Moabitess'.

items.q: Rahab hid the two spies under stalks of flax on her roof.
items.x: She hid them 'with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof'.

items.q: Moses was barred from Canaan after the incident of striking the rock.
items.x: After Moses smote the rock twice at Meribah, God said he would not bring the congregation into the land.

items.q: The fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5 lists exactly nine qualities.
items.x: Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: nine.

items.q: Moses put a veil over his face because it shone.
items.x: His face shone after speaking with God, so he put a vail on his face.

items.q: Elisha asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.
items.x: Elisha asked, 'let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me'.

items.q: 'The borrower is servant to the lender' is in Proverbs.
items.x: Proverbs 22:7: 'the borrower is servant to the lender'.

items.q: Judas Iscariot kept the money bag for the disciples.
items.x: John says Judas 'had the bag' and was a thief.

items.q: Paul was shipwrecked on an island called Melita.
items.x: After the shipwreck they learned the island was called Melita.

items.q: On Melita, a viper fastened on Paul's hand and he felt no harm.
items.x: He shook the viper into the fire and felt no harm.

items.q: Solomon had seven hundred wives.
items.x: 1 Kings 11:3: seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines.

items.q: Job lived in the land of Uz.
items.x: Job 1:1 places him in the land of Uz.

items.q: The woman at the well had had five husbands.
items.x: Jesus told her, 'thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband'.

items.q: Lazarus had been dead four days when Jesus raised him.
items.x: Martha said, 'by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days'.

items.q: Jesus was asleep on a pillow in the hinder part of the ship during the storm.
items.x: Mark alone mentions the pillow in the stern.

items.q: Lot was the son of Abram's brother Haran.
items.x: Terah begat Abram, Nahor and Haran; 'and Haran begat Lot'.

items.q: Sarah laughed within herself when she heard she would bear a son.
items.x: Sarah laughed within herself, being old.

items.q: King Saul consulted a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor.
items.x: Saul sought the woman at Endor before his last battle.

items.q: A donkey (ass) spoke to the prophet Balaam.
items.x: The LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she spoke to Balaam.

items.q: Peter's wife's mother was healed of a fever by Jesus.
items.x: Jesus touched her hand and the fever left her, so Peter was married.

items.q: Gideon's army was cut down to three hundred men.
items.x: God saved Israel by the 300 who lapped the water.

items.q: Jesus wrote with His finger on the ground when the woman taken in adultery was brought to Him.
items.x: John 8:6 says Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground.

items.q: Paul says he received thirty-nine stripes from the Jews three times.
items.x: It was FIVE times that he received forty stripes save one. He was beaten with rods three times.

items.q: Samuel anointed David king while Saul was still reigning.
items.x: Samuel anointed David in Bethlehem long before Saul's death.

items.q: The Bible says that Joseph was sold into Egypt for twenty pieces of silver.
items.x: Genesis 37:28 says he was sold to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver, and Joseph later told his brothers, 'ye sold me hither' (Genesis 45:5).

items.q: Jesus was in the tomb for exactly seven days.
items.x: Jesus said He would be raised again 'the third day'.

items.q: According to Genesis, God rested on the sixth day.
items.x: God rested on the seventh day.

items.q: Peter is the disciple who walked on water toward Jesus.
items.x: Peter came down out of the ship and walked on the water to go to Jesus.

items.q: The Bible names Pilate's wife.
items.x: Pilate's wife sent him a message about her dream, but she is not named.

items.q: John the Baptist ate locusts and wild honey.
items.x: Matthew 3:4: 'his meat was locusts and wild honey'.

items.q: King David was the youngest son of Jesse.
items.x: Jesse said, 'There remaineth yet the youngest'.

items.q: The Bible says Delilah cut Samson's hair herself.
items.x: Delilah 'called for a man' who shaved off the seven locks.

items.q: Absalom was caught by his head in the boughs of an oak.
items.x: The text says 'his head caught hold of the oak'. It doesn't say his hair, though many assume it.

items.q: Jesus' family fled to Egypt when He was a child.
items.x: Joseph took the young child and his mother into Egypt to escape Herod.

items.q: Paul and Barnabas parted ways over John Mark.
items.x: They disagreed sharply over taking Mark, and parted.
